import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Latin Tableau Conjecture

The Latin Tableau Conjecture states that the graph associated
to any (finite) Young diagram (i.e., whose vertices are the
cells of the diagram, with edges between cells in the same row
or column) is CDS-colorable, meaning that there exists a proper
coloring of the vertices of the graph such that for all k > 0, the
number of vertices with color < k equals the maximum size of
the union of k independent sets of the graph.

*References:*

* [The Latin Tableau Conjecture](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/v32i2p48)
-/

namespace LatinTableau

variable {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]

namespace SimpleGraph

/-- The Latin Tableau Conjecture: If G is the simple graph
  of a Young diagram, then G is CDS-colorable. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem LatinTableauConjecture (μ : YoungDiagram) :
     μ.toSimpleGraph.CDSColorable := by sorry

reformulations.difference: The paper initially states that a Latin tableau of shape λ and type μ exists exactly when the chromatic difference sequence δ dominates μ. Lean instead asserts CDS-colorability of every Young diagram's associated graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proper colorings of the partition graph are exactly Latin tableaux. Proposition 3 establishes that δ is a partition. The original criterion therefore implies a tableau of type δ by taking μ = δ. Conversely, Proposition 5 shows that realizable types are downward closed in dominance order, so realizing δ realizes every dominated type; necessity follows from the definition of the maximum union sizes. The paper explicitly states this equivalence after Proposition 3 and in Corollary 6. Lean's finite lower-set representation covers all partition diagrams; its empty diagram also satisfies the condition.

reformulations.difference: This imported definition requires one coloring whose first k color classes have total size α_k for every natural k, rather than explicitly sorting class sizes and equating them to δ_i = α_i − α_{i−1}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The prefix equations imply that class k has size α_{k+1} − α_k. They also force class sizes to be nonincreasing: replacing a prefix's final class by a larger later class would exceed the defining maximum. Conversely, sorted class sizes equal to these differences telescope to the prefix equations because α_0 = 0. A coloring realizing the paper's sorted shape can be relabelled in size order starting at zero. The scratch file proves the equivalence with sorted, labelled difference-size equations, and separately proves that the k = 0 condition is automatic.

reformulations.difference: This imported helper allows overlapping independent sets and uses a natural-number supremum, while Definition 1 describes the maximum cardinality of a union of disjoint independent sets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Replace each set S_i by S_i minus the union of earlier sets. This preserves independence and the overall union while making the family pairwise disjoint; the scratch file proves equality of the two suprema. Every vertex set used by the conjecture is finite, so all ncard values are genuine finite cardinalities. The attainable-size set contains zero and is bounded by the vertex count; its natural-number supremum is therefore attained. Both nonemptiness and boundedness, and attainment, were proved in Lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v32i2p48/pdf — Chow and Tiefenbruck, The Latin Tableau Conjecture, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 32(2) (2025), #P2.48; especially §§1–2, Definitions 1–2, Propositions 3 and 5, Corollary 6, and §§4–5.

Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/YoungDiagram.lean; FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Coloring/Vertex.lean; Mathlib's YoungDiagram, SimpleGraph.fromRel, Coloring, IsIndepSet, and Set.ncard definitions.
review.notes: Checked the sole theorem and its elaborated quantifiers, graph adjacency, coloring semantics, cardinalities, and boundary cases. There are no answer slots, variants, or formal_proof claims in the file. The published paper proves only partial CDS-colorability and continues to call the full conjecture open, consistent with the tag. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles and contains independent proofs of the semantic equivalences, the empty-diagram case, and correctness of a finite enumeration used to test singleton, row, column, hook, square, and (4,2,1) diagrams. The checked equivalence and enumeration proofs do not depend on sorryAx.
